N-6.1 RSTREASON bits are reset only by ext_rst_n. They survive watchdog ...
details: RSTREASON bits are reset only by ext_rst_n. They survive watchdog, debug and software resets, because a reason register cleared by the reset it records is useless.

NAME: N-6.2 Exactly one of bits 0 3 is set by any given reset. Bit 4 is set by...
details: Exactly one of bits 0–3 is set by any given reset. Bit 4 is set by software and is orthogonal.

NAME: N-6.3 Writing 1 to a bit clears it. Writing 0 has no effect.
details: Writing 1 to a bit clears it. Writing 0 has no effect.

NAME: N-6.4 A DIVSEL write takes effect only at the next pclk_phase boundary a...
details: A DIVSEL write takes effect only at the next pclk_phase boundary, and the divider transitions glitch-free (§7.5). Changing DIVSEL changes hclk and therefore all peripheral baud rates and both timer rates. Firmware is responsible for reconfiguring them.

NAME: N-6.5 DIVSEL is not reset by SWRST so a software reset does not silently...
details: DIVSEL is not reset by SWRST, so a software reset does not silently restore 250 MHz after firmware has stepped down to a lower frequency.

NAME: 7 Functional description
N-7.1 hclk at DIV=2 is generated by a single toggle flop clocked by refclk
details: hclk at DIV=2 is generated by a single toggle flop clocked by refclk:

NAME: N-7.2 A toggle flop is used rather than a clock gate. A gate that passes...
details: A toggle flop is used rather than a clock gate. A gate that passes every other reference pulse produces a 2 ns high time in an 8 ns period — 25% duty — which halves the usable setup window for every negative-edge-sensitive element and distorts hold margins. A toggle flop gives exactly 50%.

NAME: N-7.3 pclk is a second toggle flop clocked by hclk giving 125 MHz at 50 ...
details: pclk is a second toggle flop clocked by hclk, giving 125 MHz at 50% duty.

NAME: N-7.4 pclk_phase_o is asserted for the one hclk cycle preceding each pclk...
details: pclk_phase_o is asserted for the one hclk cycle preceding each pclk rising edge. The bridge uses it to know which hclk edge is safe for transfer between the two clocks. This single bit is why no clock-domain-crossing logic is needed anywhere in the chip between hclk and pclk:

NAME: N-7.5 Ratio changes are glitch-free on a DIVSEL write DIVBUSY sets the...
details: Ratio changes are glitch-free: on a DIVSEL write, DIVBUSY sets, the divider output is held at its current level until the counter reaches a state where the new ratio's edge aligns, then the new ratio takes effect. No output pulse is shorter than the shorter of the two ratios' half-periods.

NAME: N-7.6 The three clocks and their relationship (values from GARUDA-SYS-001)
details: The three clocks and their relationship (values from GARUDA-SYS-001):

NAME: N-7.7 All reset requests pass through a 1024-cycle down counter clocked b...
details: All reset requests pass through a 1024-cycle down counter clocked by refclk. A request loads the counter; the reset output stays asserted until the counter reaches zero.

NAME: N-7.8 The stretch counter is clocked by refclk not hclk. This is load-be...
details: The stretch counter is clocked by refclk, not hclk. This is load-bearing. clk_div's divider is held in reset while reset is asserted (§7.4), so hclk is not running during reset. A stretch counter on hclk would never advance, and reset would never release. refclk comes directly from the pad and runs unconditionally.

NAME: N-7.9 Without the stretch an internally generated reset is self-cancelli...
details: Without the stretch, an internally generated reset is self-cancelling. The watchdog asserts wdt_rst_req; that resets the watchdog; the watchdog stops asserting; the reset deasserts — one flop delay later. A pulse that short does not reliably reset a flop, let alone a chip, and it is invisible in RTL simulation where...

NAME: N-7.10 A new request arriving while the counter is running reloads it. Res...
details: A new request arriving while the counter is running reloads it. Resets extend; they do not queue.

NAME: N-7.11 The reset domain of each source
details: The reset domain of each source:

NAME: N-7.12 The watchdog s request flop is in the ext_rst_n domain. GARUDA-TIME...
details: The watchdog's request flop is in the ext_rst_n domain. GARUDA-TIMERS-SPEC-001 §9 states this on the watchdog side; both documents must agree, and GARUDA-SYS-001 reset.sources[wdt_rst_n].resets is the authority.

NAME: N-7.13 hartreset does not pass through the stretch counter. It is a level...
details: hartreset does not pass through the stretch counter. It is a level from the Debug Module, held as long as the debugger holds it, and is released synchronously to hclk.

NAME: N-7.14 Assertion is asynchronous. ext_rst_n reaches every flop s asynchron...
details: Assertion is asynchronous. ext_rst_n reaches every flop's asynchronous reset input without waiting for a clock, because at power-on there is no clock to wait for.

NAME: N-7.15 Release is synchronous through a two-flop synchroniser in the targ...
details: Release is synchronous, through a two-flop synchroniser in the target domain: one for hclk, one for pclk. This prevents flops in the same domain from leaving reset on different cycles, which is how a reset-release race produces a state machine in an illegal state.

NAME: N-7.16 clk_div s divider flops use raw_rst_n ext_rst_n directly unstret...
details: clk_div's divider flops use raw_rst_n — ext_rst_n directly, unstretched and unsynchronised. They cannot use the stretched output because that output depends on refclk only, while the divider must be in a known state before hclk exists at all. This is the one deliberate exception to [N-7.15] and it is safe because th...

NAME: N-7.17 Release order is refclk domain then hclk then pclk. pclk is last...
details: Release order is refclk domain, then hclk, then pclk. pclk is last because it is the slowest, so a peripheral can never see its bus interface active before its own reset has released.

NAME: N-7.18 Total reset time from ext_rst_n release to first instruction fetch...
details: Total reset time from ext_rst_n release to first instruction fetch is approximately 2.1 µs at DIV=2. Nothing in the system depends on this being short.

NAME: N-7.19 clkdiv_toggle_hclk shall be placed adjacent to the refclk pad. The...
details: clkdiv_toggle_hclk shall be placed adjacent to the refclk pad. The refclk net shall connect the pad's input buffer to that flop's clock input and to nothing else.

NAME: N-7.20 Rationale and why this is in a design document rather than left to...
details: Rationale, and why this is in a design document rather than left to physical design: 500 MHz is a 2 ns period, and this is a 1.45 mm die with a bond-wire package. A 500 MHz net routed across the die would need its own insertion-delay budget, would couple into neighbours, and would make the reference clock's duty dis...

NAME: N-7.21 clkdiv_toggle_hclk is constrained at 500 MHz (2 ns period) and shal...
details: clkdiv_toggle_hclk is constrained at 500 MHz (2 ns period) and shall be excluded from the hclk constraint set. Its timing path is a single flop with its output inverted back to its own input — no combinational logic in between — which is the simplest path that exists, and it will close. But it must be told to the ti...

NAME: 9 Clock reset and power
N-9.1 hclk and pclk are synchronous to each other ( 7.4). The only genuin...
details: hclk and pclk are synchronous to each other (§7.4). The only genuinely asynchronous boundary in the chip is tck ↔ hclk, inside the Debug Module.

NAME: N-9.2 clk_div provides no clock gating. The per-block gates (core WFI DS...
details: clk_div provides no clock gating. The per-block gates (core WFI, DSU idle, DMA per-channel, APB per-window) are defined in their own specs and gate these root clocks locally.

NAME: N-9.3 pclk at half hclk is itself a power measure it halves the dynamic...
details: pclk at half hclk is itself a power measure: it halves the dynamic power of the entire peripheral clock tree and of every peripheral flop, which is the majority of the chip's flop count outside the core. This is the reason pclk exists as a real divided clock rather than an access-rate trick — an enable scheme would...

NAME: N-9.4 No power domains no isolation cells no level shifters no retenti...
details: No power domains, no isolation cells, no level shifters, no retention flops, no voltage scaling. DIVSEL provides frequency scaling as a coarse, firmware-driven fallback and is not a dynamic power-management mechanism.

N-4.1 All macro instantiations are confined to sram_wrapper.v with this...
details: All macro instantiations are confined to sram_wrapper.v, with this interface and no other:

NAME: N-4.2 No sleep retain light-sleep ECC redundancy-repair or test-mode...
details: No sleep, retain, light-sleep, ECC, redundancy-repair or test-mode pin is assumed to exist. If the chosen compiler provides them, they are tied to their inactive state inside sram_wrapper.v and nowhere else. Rationale: the design must not be blocked on which macro options the compiler run produces, and a power savin...

NAME: N-4.3 sram_wrapper.v has a behavioural model for simulation selected by...
details: sram_wrapper.v has a behavioural model for simulation, selected by ifdef SIM_SRAM . It is byte-enable accurate and drives X on an uninitialised read, so firmware that reads uninitialised memory fails in simulation rather than passing by luck.

NAME: 6 Register map mem_ctl
N-6.1 ILOCK is write-1-to-set and sticky. There is no software path to cl...
details: ILOCK is write-1-to-set and sticky. There is no software path to clear it. It clears only on hreset_n deassertion.

NAME: N-6.2 Rationale for no software clear the bit exists to make instruction...
details: Rationale for no software clear: the bit exists to make instruction memory immutable during flight. A bit that firmware can clear is a bit that a wild pointer can clear, which defeats the purpose. Legitimate reasons to write ISRAM again — reflashing, recovery — all involve a reset, and reset clears it.

NAME: 7 Functional description
N-7.1 Region decode is performed by ahb_decoder on HADDR 31 28 per GARUD...
details: Region decode is performed by ahb_decoder on HADDR[31:28] per GARUDA-AHB-SPEC-001. Within a region, each slave decodes the low bits of its own size and ignores the rest. Values from GARUDA-SYS-001:

NAME: N-7.2 Addresses above a region s size but inside its 256 MiB decode granu...
details: Addresses above a region's size but inside its 256 MiB decode granule alias down (the high bits are ignored). This is deliberate: alias-free decode would need a range comparator per slave for no benefit, and the linker never emits such an address. An out-of-region address produces ERROR from the default slave instead.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (2 citations). // aliasing inside the 256 MiB granule [N-7.2]

NAME: N-7.3 All three memories support word halfword and byte accesses. hsize_...
details: All three memories support word, halfword and byte accesses. hsize_i and haddr_i[1:0] generate byte enables:

NAME: N-7.4 Misaligned accesses (WORD with haddr 1 0 = 00 HALF with haddr 0 ...
details: Misaligned accesses (WORD with haddr[1:0] != 00, HALF with haddr[0] != 0) never reach the slaves: the core detects them and raises a precise misaligned exception before the transfer is issued. A slave that nevertheless sees one responds ERROR, as a backstop against a defective master.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (1 citation). check(u_m.r_resp[0] && u_m.r_resp[1], "[N-7.4] misaligned word/half - ERROR");

NAME: N-7.5 Sub-word accesses to Boot ROM are permitted and read the containing...
details: Sub-word accesses to Boot ROM are permitted and read the containing word with the appropriate bytes selected, because .rodata in the ROM may be byte-addressed.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (1 citation). check(u_m.r_data[5][31:16] == 16'hB000, "Boot ROM halfword read is legal [N-7.5]");

NAME: N-7.6 All three memories are zero-wait-state hreadyout_o is held high co...
details: All three memories are zero-wait-state: hreadyout_o is held high continuously. The macro's read data arrives one cycle after the address, which lines up exactly with the AHB address-phase/data-phase split — the address is registered in the address phase and the data appears in the data phase with no stall inserted.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (2 citations). // zero wait states on every legal access [N-7.6]

NAME: N-7.7 This is only achievable if the macros meet the 4 ns cycle with the...
details: This is only achievable if the macros meet the 4 ns cycle with the AHB address multiplexing in front of them. If the compiler run shows they do not, the recovery is DIVSEL=1 (125 MHz) per ADR-0001, not a wait state, because a wait state on instruction fetch costs performance on every cycle of the flight loop.

NAME: N-7.8 When ILOCK is set a write transfer to the ISRAM region with hsel_i...
details: When ILOCK is set, a write transfer to the ISRAM region with hsel_i asserted produces a two-cycle ERROR response, and no data is written to the macro.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (3 citations). // ILOCK refuses writes, SBA bypasses, reads ok [N-7.8]..[N-7.10]

NAME: N-7.9 The lock is bypassed when hmaster_is_sba_i is asserted that is w...
details: The lock is bypassed when hmaster_is_sba_i is asserted — that is, when the Debug Module is the granted master. Rationale: the lock's purpose is to protect against a firmware bug, and the debugger is outside that threat model. Without the bypass, a chip that has locked ISRAM and then hung could not be recovered over...
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (1 citation). check(!u_m.r_resp[3] && u_m.r_data[4] == 32'h5BA0_5BA0, "[N-7.9] SBA write bypasses ILOCK");

NAME: N-7.10 Reads are never affected by ILOCK.
details: Reads are never affected by ILOCK.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (2 citations). // ILOCK refuses writes, SBA bypasses, reads ok [N-7.8]..[N-7.10]

NAME: N-7.11 Four 16 KiB macros selected by haddr 15 14 behind one AHB slave...
details: Four 16 KiB macros, selected by haddr[15:14], behind one AHB slave port. The region is contiguous: 0x2000_0000–0x2000_FFFF.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/mem/tb_mem_subsystem.sv (1 citation). // DSRAM bank decode on haddr[15:14] [N-7.11]

NAME: N-7.12 There is no bank-level concurrency. With a single shared AHB layer...
details: There is no bank-level concurrency. With a single shared AHB layer (ADR-0004) only one master holds the bus at a time, so concurrent bank access is unreachable and four separate slave ports would only add three sets of hrdata/hreadyout to multiplex.

NAME: N-7.13 Bank selection is combinational from the registered address. All fo...
details: Bank selection is combinational from the registered address. All four macros receive the same address and write data; only the selected macro's write enable is asserted, and the read multiplex selects the corresponding rdata.

NAME: N-7.14 Contiguity is a linker requirement not a preference a single heap...
details: Contiguity is a linker requirement, not a preference: a single heap growing up and a single stack growing down cannot span a fragmented region.

NAME: N-7.15 SRAM contents are undefined after reset. Macros do not reset their...
details: SRAM contents are undefined after reset. Macros do not reset their arrays.

NAME: N-7.16 Consequently .bss zeroing is firmware s job (crt0) not the bootlo...
details: Consequently, .bss zeroing is firmware's job (crt0), not the bootloader's. The bootloader copies only what has an initial value; zeroing 64 KiB in the boot ROM would waste boot time on memory the firmware may not all use.

NAME: 8 Boot
N-8.1 MAGIC is checked first. An erased flash reads 0xFFFFFFFF so a blan...
details: MAGIC is checked first. An erased flash reads 0xFFFFFFFF, so a blank board takes the recovery path rather than attempting to execute erased memory.

NAME: N-8.2 Step 9 is executable because the core s data port can read ISRAM (A...
details: Step 9 is executable because the core's data port can read ISRAM (ADR-0005). In the Rev 1.2 design it was not: the data port had no path to ISRAM, so no master in the chip could perform that read, and the CRC step could not have been implemented.

NAME: N-8.3 Step 8 was absent from Rev 1.2 entirely. Without it every initiali...
details: Step 8 was absent from Rev 1.2 entirely. Without it, every initialised global variable in the firmware holds undefined data at main().

NAME: N-8.4 The recovery loop at step 12 is nop nop j loop rather than a wfi...
details: The recovery loop at step 12 is nop; nop; j loop rather than a wfi or a halt, so the core is fetching and the bus is quiet but alive, which is the state SBA needs.

NAME: N-8.5 Each flash word is read by write the command byte to the SPI data...
details: Each flash word is read by: write the command byte to the SPI data register, poll the status register for completion, write the address bytes, poll, then write four dummy bytes and read four received bytes, polling each. Roughly 20 instructions per word.

NAME: N-8.6 64 KiB is 16 384 words so about 330 000 instructions plus SPI wir...
details: 64 KiB is 16,384 words, so about 330,000 instructions, plus SPI wire time at 20 MHz SCLK: about 8 bits × 4 bytes per word × 16,384 = 524,288 bit times ≈ 26 ms. Boot takes tens of milliseconds, once, at power-on. Nothing in the system cares.

details: MEASURED, 2026-09-23 — the estimate above is 2.6x optimistic. The flash boot path is now built and make test_chip_flash runs it. A 32-bit word costs 64 SCLK, not 32: eight command bits and twenty-four address bits precede every thirty-two data bits, because spim_read_word() issues one command per word. At the boot C...

NAME: N-8.7 The DMA alternative was rejected because a P2M transfer from the SP...
details: The DMA alternative was rejected because a P2M transfer from the SPI master requires that peripheral's data register to produce a new byte per read without a per-byte command sequence, and no document in this project had verified that the sourced IP behaves that way. (That gap is now closed in the other direction: G...

NAME: N-8.8 CRC-32-IEEE-802.3 polynomial 0x04C11DB7 initial value 0xFFFFFFFF ...
details: CRC-32/IEEE-802.3: polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, reflected input and output, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF. Computed bitwise, no lookup table — a 256-entry table would consume a quarter of the 4 KiB ROM.

NAME: N-8.9 CRC-32 rather than CRC-16 the loop is the same shape and the same...
details: CRC-32 rather than CRC-16: the loop is the same shape and the same ROM cost, and over a 64 KiB image the undetected-error probability goes from 2⁻¹⁶ to 2⁻³².

NAME: N-8.10 Bitwise CRC-32 over 64 KiB is roughly 8 cycles per bit 524 288 bi...
details: Bitwise CRC-32 over 64 KiB is roughly 8 cycles per bit × 524,288 bits ≈ 4 M cycles ≈ 17 ms at 250 MHz. Acceptable for the same reason as [N-8.6].

NAME: N-8.10a MEASURED the built ROM is 820 bytes (205 words of 1024) against t...
details: MEASURED: the built ROM is 820 bytes (205 words of 1024), against this ~500-byte estimate. The difference is mostly the bounded spin loops in sw/bootrom/spim.c — every wait there has a timeout so a dead SPI bus fails MAGIC and lands in boot_fail() instead of hanging until the watchdog. Still 20% of the budget.

NAME: N-8.11 The remaining ROM is filled with an illegal-instruction pattern (0x...
details: The remaining ROM is filled with an illegal-instruction pattern (0x00000000), so a jump into unused ROM raises an illegal-instruction exception rather than executing whatever the mask happens to contain.

NAME: N-8.12 The ROM installs a minimal trap handler at a fixed ROM address and...
details: The ROM installs a minimal trap handler at a fixed ROM address and points mtvec at it before touching the SPI. Any exception during boot sets RSTREASON.BOOTFAIL and branches to the recovery loop. details: WFI in EX asserts H5, holding the pipeline. The core wakes when clic_irq_valid_i (with that source enabled) or mtip_i is asserted — regardless of mstatus.MIE, as the privileged specification requires. If MIE is clear the core resumes at the instruction after WFI without taking a trap.

details: pipe_ctrl exports a single quiescent signal, asserted when the pipeline is held by H5 and no bus transfer is outstanding. core_clk_gate uses exactly this signal, through a standard ICG, to gate hclk to the core and DSU.

NAME: N-7.29 The gate s enable is quiescent from pipe_ctrl not a separate decod...
details: The gate's enable is quiescent from pipe_ctrl, not a separate decode of the WFI instruction. This is normative and it is the whole reason §7.6 is written as a single table. A second piece of logic deciding "the core is idle" would be a second opinion about pipeline state, and the first time the two disagreed — a flu...

NAME: N-7.30 Wake takes one cycle to ungate the clock. Total WFI wake latency is...
details: Wake takes one cycle to ungate the clock. Total WFI wake latency is 2 cycles: one to ungate, one to resume fetch. At 4 ns that is 8 ns against a 4 ms loop period.

NAME: N-7.31 The wake condition is combinational from clic_irq_valid_i and mtip_...
details: The wake condition is combinational from clic_irq_valid_i and mtip_i, which are outside the gated domain. A gated clock cannot be woken by logic inside the gated domain, so the wake term is deliberately outside it.

NAME: N-7.32 Power firmware s loop is compute-then-WFI so the core and DSU clo...
details: Power: firmware's loop is compute-then-WFI, so the core and DSU clock trees are off for most of each iteration. This is the largest single power saving in the chip, since the core and DSU hold the majority of the design's flops. The actual duty cycle is a firmware measurement ([N-6.2]) and is not asserted here.

NAME: N-7.33 core_rst_n_i and hartreset_n_i are ORed internally. Either produces...
details: core_rst_n_i and hartreset_n_i are ORed internally. Either produces a full core and DSU reset.

NAME: N-7.34 On reset the PC is BOOTROM_BASE (0x1000_0000) from the generated h...
details: On reset the PC is BOOTROM_BASE (0x1000_0000), from the generated header. The prefetch buffer is empty, all CSRs take their reset values, and mtvec is uninitialised — which is why the bootloader installs a trap handler before touching the SPI (GARUDA-MEM-SPEC-001 §8.6).

NAME: N-7.35 hartreset does not reset the bus memories or peripherals so the D...
details: hartreset does not reset the bus, memories or peripherals, so the Debug Module's SBA keeps working while the core is held. Resume is release of hartreset, and the core restarts from the reset vector — it does not continue from where it was (GARUDA-DEBUG-SPEC-001 [N-7.9]).

NAME: N-7.36 Target 250 MHz (4 ns) at DIV=2. The critical path is the 33 33 mult...
details: Target 250 MHz (4 ns) at DIV=2. The critical path is the 33×33 multiplier in series with the EX result multiplexer, with the DSU in the same cone.

NAME: N-7.37 Closure is not asserted by this document. If synthesis and place-an...
details: Closure is not asserted by this document. If synthesis and place-and-route show it does not close, the recovery is DIVSEL = 1 (DIV=4, 125 MHz) per ADR-0001 — a parameter change in clk_div, with no change to this core. At 125 MHz the loop budget is 125,000 cycles, still far more than the workload needs.

NAME: N-7.38 Stating the fallback in advance is deliberate a timing miss discov...
details: Stating the fallback in advance is deliberate: a timing miss discovered after the GDSII handoff is a schedule problem only if the recovery has to be invented then.

NAME: 5 Interfaces
N-5.1 The DSU is in the core s EX timing cone in parallel with the 33 33...
details: The DSU is in the core's EX timing cone, in parallel with the 33×33 multiplier. Both contribute to the 250 MHz question (GARUDA-CORE-SPEC-001 §7.9).

NAME: 6 Numeric contract normative
N-6.1 This section is the authority on DSU number formats. Firmware the...
details: This section is the authority on DSU number formats. Firmware, the RTL and the testbench all follow it. It did not exist before Rev 3.0.

NAME: N-6.2 Operand extraction MAC uses the low 16 bits of rs1_i and rs2_i in...
details: Operand extraction: MAC uses the low 16 bits of rs1_i and rs2_i, interpreted as signed Q1.15. The upper 16 bits are ignored, not checked. Firmware packs two Q1.15 values per 32-bit word where useful.

NAME: N-6.3 The product s 30 fractional bits align exactly with the accumulator...
details: The product's 30 fractional bits align exactly with the accumulator's 30 fractional bits, so accumulation is a plain 48-bit add with no shift. This is why Q18.30 was chosen rather than a format requiring realignment on every accumulate — a shifter in the accumulate path would land in the EX critical cone.

NAME: N-6.4 Headroom 18 integer bits against a product magnitude below 2.0 all...
details: Headroom: 18 integer bits against a product magnitude below 2.0 allows 2¹⁷ = 131,072 accumulations before the integer field can overflow, worst case. Practical loops here accumulate 10 to 50 terms.

NAME: N-6.5 Q1.15 operands are restricted to ( 1 +1). Any value outside that r...
details: Q1.15 operands are restricted to (−1, +1). Any value outside that range must be scaled by firmware before it reaches the DSU. The unit does not check, and an out-of-range operand is silently reinterpreted — a wrapped Q1.15 value, not a saturated one.

NAME: N-6.6 This is the load-bearing limitation and the reason 7.5 exists. A q...
details: This is the load-bearing limitation and the reason §7.5 exists. A quantity with a dynamic range wider than about 2¹⁵ relative steps cannot be represented in Q1.15 at fixed scaling, and an EKF covariance matrix has exactly that problem: diagonal terms span many orders of magnitude as the filter converges.

NAME: N-6.7 On accumulate if the 49-bit intermediate sum exceeds the 48-bit si...
details: On accumulate, if the 49-bit intermediate sum exceeds the 48-bit signed range, the accumulator saturates to 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF (positive) or 0x8000_0000_0000 (negative), and the sticky overflow flag for that accumulator sets.

NAME: N-6.8 Saturation rather than wrap a wrapped accumulator changes sign so...
details: Saturation rather than wrap: a wrapped accumulator changes sign, so an APF repulsion force would reverse direction and push the vehicle toward the obstacle. Saturation gives a wrong magnitude in the right direction, which degrades rather than inverts.

NAME: N-6.9 The overflow flag is sticky and set-beats-clear a MACCLEAR in the...
details: The overflow flag is sticky and set-beats-clear: a MACCLEAR in the same cycle as an overflow leaves the flag set. Firmware must check it after a computation, not assume its own clear won.

NAME: 7 Functional description
N-7.1 Every instruction is single-cycle throughput. The only stall is the...
details: Every instruction is single-cycle throughput. The only stall is the same-accumulator RAW interlock (§7.3).

NAME: N-7.2 MACDOT is the EKF and APF primitive it issues two 16 16 products i...
details: MACDOT is the EKF and APF primitive: it issues two 16×16 products into two different accumulators in one instruction, which is what makes a 2-element dot product one cycle rather than two.

NAME: N-7.3 MACSAT converts an accumulator back to Q1.15 with saturation which...
details: MACSAT converts an accumulator back to Q1.15 with saturation, which is the normal way a result re-enters the RV32IM datapath. MACREAD_LO/_HI give the raw Q18.30 value for firmware that needs the full precision or is writing diagnostics.

NAME: N-7.4 acc_sel = 2 b11 raises an illegal-instruction exception in every in...
details: acc_sel = 2'b11 raises an illegal-instruction exception in every instruction that carries the field (R-7). It does not alias to ACC_MAG, and it does not silently do nothing.

NAME: N-7.5 Rationale an illegal encoding that aliases to a real accumulator t...
details: Rationale: an illegal encoding that aliases to a real accumulator turns an assembler bug or a corrupted instruction word into a silent wrong answer in the flight computation. Raising the exception makes it a precise fault with mtval = the instruction.

NAME: N-7.6 An accumulator write has a one-cycle result latency. An instruction...
details: An accumulator write has a one-cycle result latency. An instruction reading the same accumulator in the next cycle — MACREAD_LO immediately after MAC, for instance — would read the stale value.

NAME: N-7.7 dsu_interlock detects this and asserts dsu_busy_o which pipe_ctrl...
details: dsu_interlock detects this and asserts dsu_busy_o, which pipe_ctrl treats as hold source H4 (GARUDA-CORE-SPEC-001 §7.6). One cycle of stall.

NAME: N-7.8 The interlock is per accumulator. A MAC on ACC_FX followed by a MAC...
details: The interlock is per accumulator. A MAC on ACC_FX followed by a MACREAD_LO on ACC_FY does not stall. This is what makes three accumulators worth having: firmware interleaves work on different accumulators and the interlock never fires.

NAME: N-7.9 dsu_busy_o is an ordinary hold source not a special case in the pi...
details: dsu_busy_o is an ordinary hold source, not a special case in the pipeline control logic. The flush-beats-hold rule of [N-7.21] in the core spec applies to it exactly as to load-use: a branch or trap concurrent with dsu_busy discards the DSU operation in EX. That matters because the accumulator must not be updated by...

NAME: N-7.10 The artificial potential field inner loop computes for each neighb...
details: The artificial potential field inner loop computes, for each neighbour, a repulsion vector inversely proportional to distance, and sums the vectors:

NAME: N-7.11 Roughly 300 cycles for 10 neighbours against 250 000 cycles per lo...
details: Roughly 300 cycles for 10 neighbours, against 250,000 cycles per loop iteration. Positions normalised to the field extent are naturally within (−1, +1), so Q1.15 is the right format for this computation and there is no scaling difficulty.

NAME: N-7.12 This is the DSU s clear unqualified win and it is the workload it...
details: This is the DSU's clear, unqualified win, and it is the workload it was designed around.

NAME: N-7.13 The DSU accelerates the parts of the EKF whose operands are bounded...
details: The DSU accelerates the parts of the EKF whose operands are bounded and well-scaled, and does not accelerate the rest. Stating which is which:

NAME: N-7.14 So the covariance path is RV32IM firmware using the core s 33 33 m...
details: So the covariance path is RV32IM firmware, using the core's 33×33 multiplier and the software divide handler. The DSU serves the prediction and residual paths.

NAME: N-7.15 This document does not claim a speedup figure for the EKF. The figu...
details: This document does not claim a speedup figure for the EKF. The figure is measurable — profile with mcycle around each stage, with and without the DSU path — and it is the single most useful number for the project's technical write-up. Until it is measured, no figure is asserted. Asserting one and being asked to defe...

NAME: N-7.16 A v2 option that would extend the DSU s reach here is block floatin...
details: A v2 option that would extend the DSU's reach here is block floating-point: a per-matrix exponent held in firmware, with MACSHIFT used to renormalise between blocks. MACSHIFT exists and is sufficient for this; it requires no hardware change, only a firmware scheme. Recorded as a possibility, not a commitment.

NAME: N-7.17 All three accumulators and all three overflow flags are continuousl...
details: All three accumulators and all three overflow flags are continuously visible to the Debug Module, with no core involvement (R-6).

NAME: N-7.18 This is the most valuable observability in the chip. With SBA-only...
details: This is the most valuable observability in the chip. With SBA-only debug there is no GPR inspection (GARUDA-DEBUG-SPEC-001 [N-7.9]), so during bring-up of the APF or EKF the accumulators are the only direct window into the arithmetic. A wrong repulsion force is visible here immediately, without instrumenting firmware.

NAME: N-7.19 The 48-bit values are read as two 32-bit halves with a coherent-sna...
details: The 48-bit values are read as two 32-bit halves with a coherent-snapshot mechanism (GARUDA-DEBUG-SPEC-001 §6.8).

NAME: N-7.20 The DSU is inside the core s WFI clock gate and additionally gated...
details: The DSU is inside the core's WFI clock gate, and additionally gated by dsu_idle — no Custom-0 instruction in EX and no interlock pending.

NAME: N-7.21 dsu_idle is derived in dsu_decode from dsu_valid_i and the interloc...
details: dsu_idle is derived in dsu_decode from dsu_valid_i and the interlock state, both of which are already registered. It is not a second opinion about pipeline state, so it does not fall foul of GARUDA-CORE-SPEC-001 [N-7.29].

NAME: N-7.22 The accumulators must retain their values while gated so they are...
details: The accumulators must retain their values while gated, so they are not reset by the gate and the gate is enable-based, never a reset. An accumulator cleared by entering an idle cycle would corrupt a computation split across a stall.

N-9.1 One clock domain hclk gated as in 7.7. No CDC.
details: One clock domain, hclk, gated as in §7.7. No CDC.

NAME: N-9.2 core_rst_n_i clears all three accumulators and all three overflow f...
details: core_rst_n_i clears all three accumulators and all three overflow flags.

NAME: N-9.3 Power three 16 16 multipliers and three 48-bit adders are a meanin...
details: Power: three 16×16 multipliers and three 48-bit adders are a meaningful share of the core's dynamic power when active, and they are active for a few hundred cycles per millisecond. dsu_idle gating is therefore worth more here than almost anywhere else in the chip, in proportion to the logic it covers.

details: The interconnect has no registers and no APB window. It is not software-visible. Bus errors surface as precise exceptions in the master that caused them, not as status bits here — a status register would be read after the fact and could not identify which access failed.

details: One shared AHB-Lite layer. Exactly one master holds the bus at a time. All four slaves see the same address and control bus, distinguished by HSEL.

details: The only permitted access restriction mechanisms in this chip are (a) address decode, (b) the ISRAM write lock, and (c) a slave's own rejection of an operation it does not support, such as a write to Boot ROM. Structural reachability restrictions — removing a wire so a master cannot address a slave — are forbidden....

This is an omission of an unused path, not an access-control mechanism, and it is recorded in GARUDA-SYS-001 so any future need for it is a one-line change there rather than a dis...

details: Within a granule, addresses above the slave's size alias down; the slave ignores the unused address bits. GARUDA-MEM-SPEC-001 [N-7.2] states the same and gives the reasoning.

NAME: N-7.14 hmaster_is_sba_o is asserted whenever the granted master is M2 and...
details: hmaster_is_sba_o is asserted whenever the granted master is M2, and is routed to the ISRAM slave only. It carries the grant, registered into the data phase alongside the transfer, so the slave evaluates it in the same cycle as the write.

details: The ERROR is returned to the granted master, which raises a precise exception: instruction access fault for M0, load or store access fault for M1. The DMA sets its channel's error status and raises its error interrupt. The SBA sets sberror.

NAME: N-7.18 The bus never hangs on an undecoded address. There is no timeout me...
details: The bus never hangs on an undecoded address. There is no timeout mechanism in the interconnect because there is no path by which a transfer can fail to terminate: every encoding of HADDR[31:28] selects either a real slave or the default slave, and the APB bridge — the only slave that can take unbounded time — has it...

NAME: N-7.19 The interconnect inserts no wait states. HREADY seen by the granted...
details: The interconnect inserts no wait states. HREADY seen by the granted master is the selected slave's hreadyout, combinationally. All three memories are zero-wait-state; only the APB bridge extends transfers.

NAME: N-7.20 An ungranted master sees HREADY low which holds it in its address...
details: An ungranted master sees HREADY low, which holds it in its address phase until granted. This is the standard AHB-Lite mechanism for stalling a master and requires no additional handshake.

NAME: 9 Clock reset and power
N-9.1 The entire interconnect is in the hclk domain. There is no clock cr...
details: The entire interconnect is in the hclk domain. There is no clock crossing inside it. The hclk↔pclk relationship is handled entirely within the APB bridge and is synchronous in any case (GARUDA-CLKRST-SPEC-001 §7.4).

NAME: N-9.2 Reset is hreset_n. On reset the arbiter grants M0 all HSEL are low...
details: Reset is hreset_n. On reset the arbiter grants M0, all HSEL are low, and HREADY is high, so an ungranted master's first request is accepted immediately rather than stalling on a bus that appears busy.

NAME: N-9.3 Power the interconnect is combinational apart from the arbiter s g...
details: Power: the interconnect is combinational apart from the arbiter's grant register, so it consumes essentially nothing when idle. No clock gating is applied. Gating the interconnect would require predicting the next request a cycle early, which is not possible and would save a handful of flops.

NAME: 11 Verification plan
N-11.1 t_ahb_reachability exists specifically so that a future attempt to...
details: t_ahb_reachability exists specifically so that a future attempt to save area by removing a master-slave path fails a test rather than silently breaking boot. The covers are the regression guard for MEM-1, and they should be treated as non-negotiable.

NAME: N-11.2 The existing regression already covers R-1 R-3 R-5 R-6 R-8 and...
details: The existing regression already covers R-1, R-3, R-5, R-6, R-8 and R-9 for three masters with zero protocol violations. Rev 4.0's incremental verification burden is M2: the SBA master, its priority position, and the hmaster_is_sba indication.

NAME: ahb2apb bridge + apb fabric (7-8)

NAME: 2 Requirements
R-1 Convert AHB-Lite transfers in the APB region to APB3 transfers.
details: Convert AHB-Lite transfers in the APB region to APB3 transfers.

NAME: R-2 Decode eleven 4 KiB windows.
details: Decode eleven 4 KiB windows.

NAME: R-3 Peripherals shall be clocked at 125 MHz not 250 MHz to halve peri...
details: Peripherals shall be clocked at 125 MHz, not 250 MHz, to halve peripheral-domain dynamic power.

NAME: R-4 No clock-domain-crossing synchronisers shall be required between hc...
details: No clock-domain-crossing synchronisers shall be required between hclk and pclk, and the reason shall be stated as a checkable property rather than asserted.

NAME: R-5 The APB access rate shall be a per-window parameter so an IP with...
details: The APB access rate shall be a per-window parameter, so an IP with a lower maximum frequency can be accommodated without a second clock.

NAME: R-6 Byte and halfword accesses shall be rejected with an error not sil...
details: Byte and halfword accesses shall be rejected with an error, not silently widened.

NAME: R-7 A peripheral that never asserts PREADY shall not hang the bus.
details: A peripheral that never asserts PREADY shall not hang the bus.

NAME: R-8 An access to an unmapped window offset shall return an error.
details: An access to an unmapped window offset shall return an error.

NAME: 5 Interfaces
N-5.1 APB_DIV is a synthesis parameter not a register. The value is a pr...
details: APB_DIV is a synthesis parameter, not a register. The value is a property of the peripheral IP instantiated in that window, fixed at integration, and a register would let firmware set a value the IP cannot meet.

NAME: 6 Register map
N-6.1 The bridge has no registers. It is transparent apart from the error...
details: The bridge has no registers. It is transparent apart from the error responses of §7.5–§7.7, which surface as precise faults in the accessing master. mem_ctl's MEMCTL register occupies offset 0x20 of window 8 and belongs to GARUDA-MEM-SPEC-001, not to the bridge.

NAME: N-6.2 0x4000_0000 (window index 0 of the old map) is unmapped it held th...
details: 0x4000_0000 (window index 0 of the old map) is unmapped: it held the SPI slave, which ADR-0020 removed for the pin budget. An access there returns SLVERR per §7.7. The address is retained as unmapped rather than compacting the map, so the 36-pin variant can reinstate the SPI slave without moving ten other base addre...

NAME: 7 Functional description
N-7.1 An AHB transfer with hsel_i high htrans_i = NONSEQ or SEQ and a l...
details: An AHB transfer with hsel_i high, htrans_i = NONSEQ or SEQ, and a legal size starts an APB transfer. The FSM runs IDLE → SETUP → ACCESS → DONE.

NAME: N-7.2 hreadyout_o is held low from acceptance until DONE stalling the AH...
details: hreadyout_o is held low from acceptance until DONE, stalling the AHB master.

NAME: N-7.3 Minimum latency is 4 pclk cycles = 8 hclk cycles = 32 ns at APB_DIV...
details: Minimum latency is 4 pclk cycles = 8 hclk cycles = 32 ns at APB_DIV=÷1. A peripheral register access therefore costs the core about 8 cycles. At 7% bus utilisation and a few dozen peripheral accesses per flight-loop iteration this is immaterial; DMA exists so that per-byte peripheral traffic does not pay it.

NAME: N-7.4 pclk is generated by a toggle flop clocked by hclk (GARUDA-CLKRST-S...
details: pclk is generated by a toggle flop clocked by hclk (GARUDA-CLKRST-SPEC-001 [N-7.3]). Therefore:

NAME: N-7.5 Consequently every transfer between the domains is sampled on an ed...
details: Consequently every transfer between the domains is sampled on an edge both domains share. There is no window in which a pclk flop samples an hclk flop mid-transition, because the two never transition at different times. Metastability requires a setup violation from an unknown phase relationship; here the phase relat...

NAME: N-7.6 STA handles this with one create_clock and two create_generated_clo...
details: STA handles this with one create_clock and two create_generated_clock statements. The hclk→pclk paths are timed as ordinary multi-cycle synchronous paths. No synchronisers, no metastability, no CDC waivers, no gray coding.

NAME: N-7.7 This is different in kind from the tck hclk boundary in the Debug M...
details: This is different in kind from the tck↔hclk boundary in the Debug Module, which is a genuine asynchronous crossing with an unrelated clock source and does require synchronisers.

NAME: N-7.8 The hclk-side capture registers load on any hclk edge and the pclk...
details: The hclk-side capture registers load on any hclk edge, and the pclk-side FSM advances only on pclk edges. The bridge uses pclk_phase_i to guarantee that the hclk side does not change the captured address or write data during the hclk cycle in which the pclk side samples it. Assertion a_capture_stable_at_phase (§10)...

NAME: N-7.9 APB_DIV extends the ACCESS phase for a window by holding PENABLE as...
details: APB_DIV extends the ACCESS phase for a window by holding PENABLE asserted for 1, 2, 4 or 8 pclk cycles before sampling PREADY.

NAME: N-7.10 This is an access-rate mechanism not a clocking mechanism. The per...
details: This is an access-rate mechanism, not a clocking mechanism. The peripheral's flops still receive pclk at 125 MHz. It therefore accommodates an IP whose interface timing needs longer phases, but not an IP whose internal logic cannot meet the 8 ns pclk period. For that case the only remedies are DIVSEL on clk_div (GAR...

NAME: N-7.11 All eleven windows default to 1 on the assumption that a simple UA...
details: All eleven windows default to ÷1 on the assumption that a simple UART, SPI or I²C block in a 28 nm process meets 125 MHz. If an IP datasheet later shows otherwise, that window's APB_DIV changes and nothing else in the chip is affected.

NAME: N-7.12 Only hsize_i = WORD (3 b010) is accepted. BYTE and HALFWORD accesse...
details: Only hsize_i = WORD (3'b010) is accepted. BYTE and HALFWORD accesses produce a two-cycle AHB ERROR without generating any APB transfer.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/ahb2apb/tb_ahb2apb.sv (1 citation). check(u_m.r_resp[0] && u_m.r_resp[1], "[N-7.12] byte and halfword rejected with ERROR");

NAME: N-7.13 Rationale APB3 has no byte enables. A bridge that accepted a byte...
details: Rationale: APB3 has no byte enables. A bridge that accepted a byte write would have to read the word, merge, and write back — three transfers for one, and a read-modify-write against a peripheral whose registers may have read side effects, clear-on-read fields or write-1-to-clear semantics. Silently doing that is wo...

NAME: N-7.14 Every peripheral register in this chip is 32 bits and word-aligned ...
details: Every peripheral register in this chip is 32 bits and word-aligned, so no correct firmware performs a sub-word peripheral access.

NAME: N-7.15 If PREADY for the selected window is not asserted within 16 pclk cy...
details: If PREADY for the selected window is not asserted within 16 pclk cycles of entering ACCESS, the bridge abandons the transfer, deasserts PSEL and PENABLE, and returns a two-cycle AHB ERROR.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/ahb2apb/tb_ahb2apb.sv (1 citation). check(u_m.r_resp[0], "[N-7.15] 16-pclk PREADY timeout - ERROR");

NAME: N-7.16 16 cycles is chosen as comfortably longer than any legitimate wait...
details: 16 cycles is chosen as comfortably longer than any legitimate wait in this peripheral set — none of them inserts more than 2 — while being short enough that a hung peripheral costs 128 ns rather than a stalled flight loop.

NAME: N-7.17 The timeout is the only thing standing between a defective or unclo...
details: The timeout is the only thing standing between a defective or unclocked peripheral and a permanently stalled bus. GARUDA-AHB-SPEC-001 [N-7.18] relies on it: the interconnect has no timeout of its own precisely because the only slave that can stall indefinitely has one here.

NAME: N-7.18 A timeout leaves the peripheral in an undefined state it may have...
details: A timeout leaves the peripheral in an undefined state — it may have latched a write. No recovery is attempted. The reasonable firmware response is to treat the access fault as fatal and reset.

NAME: N-7.19 haddr 15 12 values with no window 0x0 (the removed SPI slave) an...
details: haddr[15:12] values with no window — 0x0 (the removed SPI slave) and 0xB–0xF — assert no PSEL and return a two-cycle AHB ERROR.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/ahb2apb/tb_ahb2apb.sv (2 citations). check(u_m.r_resp[2] && u_m.r_resp[3], "[N-7.19] window 0 and 0xC unmapped - ERROR");

NAME: N-7.20 A window asserting PSLVERR with PREADY causes the bridge to return...
details: A window asserting PSLVERR with PREADY causes the bridge to return a two-cycle AHB ERROR. Peripherals assert PSLVERR for unmapped offsets within their own window and for illegal field writes, as defined in each peripheral's own specification.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/ahb2apb/tb_ahb2apb.sv (1 citation). check(u_m.r_resp[0], "[N-7.20] PSLVERR - ERROR");

NAME: N-7.21 All three error sources sub-word unmapped window PSLVERR prod...
details: All three error sources — sub-word, unmapped window, PSLVERR — produce the identical AHB two-cycle ERROR. The master cannot distinguish them, and does not need to: all three are firmware bugs, and mepc identifies the instruction.

NAME: 9 Clock reset and power
N-9.1 The bridge is the only block in the chip spanning hclk and pclk. Bo...
details: The bridge is the only block in the chip spanning hclk and pclk. Both are synchronous (§7.2). tck does not appear here.

NAME: N-9.2 hreadyout_o resets to 0 not 1. The bridge spans two reset releases...
details: hreadyout_o resets to 0, not 1. The bridge spans two reset releases: hreset_n deasserts two hclk cycles after the stretch counter expires, preset_n two pclk cycles after that (GARUDA-CLKRST-SPEC-001 §7.17). Between those two moments the AHB side is live and the APB side is still in reset. Resetting hreadyout_o low h...

NAME: N-9.3 hreadyout_o is released only when both hreset_n_i and the synchroni...
details: hreadyout_o is released only when both hreset_n_i and the synchronised preset_n_i are deasserted. This is the requirement GARUDA-CLKRST-SPEC-001 §5.2 refers to.
implementation_note: CHECKED: tb/ahb2apb/tb_ahb2apb.sv (1 citation). check(hreadyout, "[N-9.3] hreadyout released after both resets");

NAME: N-9.4 Power the pclk domain at half hclk halves the dynamic power of the...
details: Power: the pclk domain at half hclk halves the dynamic power of the peripheral clock tree and of every peripheral flop, which together are the largest flop population outside the core. This is the whole reason pclk exists as a real divided clock rather than an access-rate trick — APB_DIV alone would deliver the same...

NAME: N-9.5 Each window s PSEL is a natural enable term for a per-peripheral cl...
details: Each window's PSEL is a natural enable term for a per-peripheral clock gate. The gate belongs to the peripheral, not the bridge, so that a peripheral with internal timers — the PWM, for instance — can keep running while unselected. The bridge exposes psel_o and makes no gating decision.

NAME: 11 Verification plan
N-11.1 t_apb_no_cdc and t_apb_reset_skew are the two tests specific to thi...
details: t_apb_no_cdc and t_apb_reset_skew are the two tests specific to this bridge's architecture rather than to APB3 in general. The first checks the property the whole chip's clocking rests on; the second covers a window that exists only because two reset releases are staggered, and that no protocol checker would look for.
